description: An account is deployed via CREATE2, self-destructs within the same transaction (fully removed per EIP-6780 since it was created this tx), and is then redeployed at the same address via a second same-tx CREATE2. The final SSR must reflect a real net delta (nonexistent -> existing) rather than being omitted by create-then-destroy pruning, since a persistent account remains at the transaction boundary.
spec_gap_note: validation_vector_spec.md's Fork Invariant governs lifecycle mechanics per fork_identifier, but no journal_action explicitly represents CREATE/SELFDESTRUCT -- lifecycle here is inferred from the combination of NONCE_MUTATION/CODE_MUTATION/BALANCE_MUTATION events on the same address. This vector is also the worked example motivating an explicit 'unless recreated later in the same transaction' clause for the create-then-destroy omission rule.

account_deltas.reason: a persistent account remains at the transaction boundary, so the create-then-destroy omission rule does not apply even though this address was also created+destroyed earlier in this same transaction

notes: original/current code_hash for the nonexistent-account case uses EMPTY_CODE_HASH rather than null: per EIP-161 state clearing, an account with nonce 0, balance 0, and empty code is indistinguishable from a nonexistent account, so this is the correct representation under this schema (which has no explicit null/nonexistent account type). The 0x4...004 current code_hash 0xf8b07b08... is the real, independently-recomputed keccak256 of the placeholder init bytecode 0x6001600155 used in this fixture -- not a fabricated value. Sender balance bundles the 5 ETH sent across both CREATE2 endowments plus illustrative gas billing, not precisely metered.
